channel.description: Latest updates from Google Developers Search team

item.title: Powering the Agent Development Lifecycle with any framework, from ADK to LangChain and beyond
item.description: The Agents CLI Extension System enables developers to use frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or custom enterprise stacks while retaining a unified deployment and evaluation workflow. It details a first-party LangChain template that scaffolds, runs, and deploys agents without requiring the Agent Development Kit (ADK). Additionally, it demonstrates how platform teams can author custom extensions to enforce policies such as automated software bill of materials (SBOM) scans during deployment.]]>

item.title: Unifying Edge AI: How Coral NPU’s open standard brings portable, energy-viable intelligence from model to silicon
item.description: Google Research has completed the 32-bit open-source Coral NPU RISC-V architecture with the introduction of its Matrix Execution Unit, which delivers up to 1 TOPS while targeting 10 mW average power for edge inference. Alongside this architecture, the release of the v1.0 open-source IREE/MLIR compiler allows developers to take models from JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow straight to Coral NPU hardware without writing custom assembly. Developers can now prototype and deploy these multimodal edge applications using new hardware options like the Synaptics Astra SR200 MCU series and globally available Coralboard devkits.12]]>

item.title: Announcing New vLLM and SGLang Inference Engines on TPU
item.description: This post announces native PyTorch backends for vLLM and SGLang powered by TorchTPU, enabling developers to run and optimize serving workloads using familiar PyTorch tools. Built in collaboration with open-source project maintainers, these engines include optimized TPU kernel implementations, production-ready features like KV cache management with TPU Sync, and disaggregated serving. Public benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and industry-leading cost efficiency on Ironwood TPU across long-context and agentic workloads.]]>

item.title: Integrating TorchTPU into TorchTitan and Optimizing Models for TPU
item.description: TorchTPU integrates a native torch.device("tpu") backend directly into PyTorch, allowing developers to train large-scale models on Google Cloud TPUs without rewriting code in JAX. The TorchTitan TPU fork enhances this with production-grade scaling primitives like SimpleFSDP, Graph Trainer, and custom Pallas kernels that achieve high Model Flops Utilization (MFU) across dense and MoE architectures. Developers can leverage these battle-tested optimization playbooks, recipes, and the Hugging Face modeling backend to efficiently scale their own workloads on TPU infrastructure.]]>

item.title: Bringing Visual Graph Debugging to Custom Edge Compilers with Model Explorer
item.description: Google AI Edge Model Explorer now supports custom compiler intermediate representations and open-source adapters like TOSA, VGF, and PTE for on-device machine learning. Developers can leverage hierarchical graph visualization, split-pane views, and per-node trace overlays to catch export regressions and verify hardware delegation. These tools enable engineering teams to transparently debug execution graphs and pinpoint cycle-level latency bottlenecks locally.]]>

item.title: Step by Step guide: Build a Voice Agent That Never Goes Silent using ADK
item.description: The open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) and gemini-3.8-live enable developers to build responsive voice agents by implementing non-blocking tools in Python. Developers can use streaming tools to yield progress updates or background execution patterns to keep conversations fluid during long-running backend queries. Additionally, configuring response scheduling behaviors such as WHEN_IDLE, INTERRUPT, or SILENT gives developers precise control over when and how tool results are delivered into the conversation.]]>

item.title: Native Model Authoring for Edge with LiteRT Tensor API
item.description: Meet the LiteRT Tensor API: giving developers native C++ control over the model graph to unify end-to-end ML computations on heterogeneous edge hardware.]]>

item.title: Announcing DPoP Support for Google OAuth: Securing Refresh Tokens
item.description: Google OAuth Platform now supports DPoP (Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession) to sender-constrain refresh tokens, neutralizing Infostealer malware and adversary-in-the-middle attacks. By cryptographically binding long-lived refresh tokens while maintaining short-lived access tokens as standard Bearer tokens, developers achieve robust credential security without incurring high-QPS API performance overhead. Additionally, developers integrating multi-agent or Model Context Protocol (MCP) workloads can use Google Cloud Secure Token Service (STS) to handle secure token delegation across agent chains.]]>

item.title: Three layers, one repo: a tour of google/adk-recipes
item.description: The google/adk-recipes repository unifies Agent Development Kit (ADK) resources into three structured layers—core/, plugins/, and contrib/—serving as a single source of truth for building AI agents. Developers can leverage reference patterns, install modular vertical skills (such as retail product search and virtual try-on) directly into their coding assistants, and deploy production-ready services across multiple languages. This cohesive structure streamlines the entire workflow from initial scaffolding to full deployment on Google Cloud infrastructure.]]>

item.title: Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
item.description: A practical engineering guide and reference architecture for establishing continuous evaluation pipelines for multi-turn AI agents using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google ADK, and OpenInference standards.]]>
